reference: Dummy review scaffold distilled from attractiveness-evidence-base.md; validate sources and wording before production.
notes: Population-average rater preferences are not personal targets or health advice.
Entries marked ship-reference may be shown as cited reference context only, never as a prescription.
Entries marked do-not-ship or needs-research should be used to explain why the app avoids hard targets.
All rows require Dawson/content review before public launch.

metrics.label: Female waist-to-hip ratio reference
metrics.populationReference: Female WHR near 0.7 appears in rater studies, but integrated proportionality matters more than a single ratio.
metrics.userFacingSummary: Use WHR as population-average context, not as a personal ideal. The app should frame changes relative to the goal the user chose.
metrics.framing: Reference only: never say a user should hit 0.7 or is deficient if they do not.
notes: Show alongside waist and hip trends rather than as a standalone score.

metrics.label: Male adiposity and BMI context
metrics.populationReference: One 2025 study rated male bodies around BMI 23-27 and 13-14 percent body fat highest across three countries.
metrics.userFacingSummary: For male physique goals, label leanness/adiposity context as emerging and avoid promising a universal ideal.
metrics.framing: Planning context only; do not diagnose body fat or rank attractiveness.
notes: Needs replication with larger and more diverse stimulus sets.
Do not convert this into a mandatory weight target.

metrics.label: Male shoulder-to-waist context
metrics.evidenceStrength: context-limited and controlled by adiposity in newer work
metrics.populationReference: Existing shoulder-to-waist findings are context-limited and should not become a hard standalone target.
metrics.userFacingSummary: Track shoulder and waist changes as the user-selected goal, but do not claim a researched ideal shoulder-to-waist ratio.
metrics.framing: Useful training metric, not an attractiveness standard.
notes: Keep workout suggestions conservative and goal-relative.
Avoid short-term desirability framing in product copy.

metrics.label: Facial averageness
metrics.populationReference: Facial averageness is consistently associated with higher rater attractiveness across multiple studies and populations.
metrics.userFacingSummary: Averageness is whole-face context, not a single face-measurement target. Keep face logs descriptive and local-only.
metrics.framing: Reference concept only; do not generate a face score or optimization target.
notes: Does not justify uploading face images.

metrics.label: Female facial femininity
metrics.populationReference: Female facial femininity is associated with attractiveness in the first-pass sources; male facial masculinity is weak or null.
metrics.userFacingSummary: If mentioned, present this as modest population-level context and avoid applying it to every user or identity.
metrics.framing: Informational only; no gender policing or identity inference.
notes: Do not ship male facial masculinity as a target.
Keep this behind local-only face measurement framing.

metrics.label: Popular face-ratio claims
metrics.populationReference: Canthal tilt, facial thirds/fifths, golden-ratio claims, and fWHR targets did not have ship-quality support in the first pass.
metrics.userFacingSummary: The app should explain that these are unsupported or contested instead of turning them into goals.
metrics.framing: Use as a safety rail for looksmaxxing traffic.
notes: Do not build presets from this row.
A dedicated follow-up research pass is needed before any popular ratio is promoted.
